purpose: Evaluate whether a private, read-only pre-meeting brief reduces repeated context gathering without creating messages, tasks, calendar changes or external commitments.

evidence.interpretation: The local processing ledger repeatedly contains meeting-preparation semantics; the count includes retries, monitors and negative examples and is not a unique-meeting count.
evidence.existingGap: The product can identify work and create a retrospective journal, but has no pre-meeting context synthesis responsibility.

dataSources: the owner's upcoming accepted or organized Lark calendar events through the existing read-only calendar capability
bounded context already available to the single Feishu consumer for the exact meeting or linked matter
existing assistant-owned task projection metadata and immutable work-journal records
explicitly linked documents and assistant knowledge already within the current workspace/read permissions

trigger.window: 15 minutes to 24 hours before an event
trigger.responsibility: owner is organizer or has an explicit direct responsibility
trigger.minimumCoverage: calendar plus at least one bounded contextual source
trigger.deduplication: one local shadow draft per opaque event revision digest

allowedActions: add a runtime-inactive meeting-briefing workflow and read-only adapters that reuse existing calendar, context, task and journal boundaries
run a 10-working-day or 8-eligible-meeting shadow pilot, whichever comes first
write only a private local redacted draft, source coverage, reason codes and evaluation counters
use existing repository and lark-cli dependencies only; install no third-party code
commit and push the implementation only after deterministic gates and the full repository check pass
explicitExclusions: send a Feishu message or any other notification, even to the owner
create or update a calendar event, task, document or external record
contact an attendee, reply in a chat, call an external research assistant or make a commitment
read unrelated conversations, entire drives or unlinked files
store raw message, document or calendar bodies in the capability ledger
add a scheduler, event consumer, provider graph, database owner or external write effect
change DSH/Cordis composition, credentials, permissions, runtime dependencies or the active LaunchAgent

success: at least 80 percent of eligible meetings produce a draft with calendar plus one contextual source
zero unrelated-source reads, raw-content persistence, duplicate revisions, notifications or external writes
manual review rates at least 70 percent of sampled drafts as materially reducing context gathering
failure: any privacy, approval, source-scope, deduplication or external-effect violation
more than 30 percent low-value or misleading drafts
source availability is insufficient to evaluate eight meetings within 10 working days

notificationPolicy: Silent for the entire revision 1 shadow pilot. Any owner-visible delivery requires a new revision and separate approval.
perInstanceConfirmation: Every attendee reply, calendar or task mutation, document write, external research call and external commitment remains individually confirmed and is not authorized by this pilot.

compatibility.local: reuse the current local-first read boundaries and SQLite-backed assistant state without a new writer
compatibility.server: keep local context unresolved on the server; only bounded counters and digests may be portable
compatibility.singleOwner: reuse the existing scheduler and single Feishu consumer; create no second consumer or writer

rollback.method: Disable the inactive pilot flag, remove the local shadow drafts and counters created by the exact pilot namespace, then revert the implementation commit.

notDoingCost: Meeting preparation remains a repeated manual context-gathering task and important decisions or open questions may be reconstructed late.
